title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail in Horizontal Drainage Lines
description: A common mistake in residential drainage installation is placing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal pipe connection. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from a horizontal branch to a vertical stack. When installed horizontally, the sharp sweep does not provide sufficient directional flow transition for solids and wastewater. This leads to frequent clogs, sluggish drainage, and potential backflow issues. Instead, plumbing codes require long-sweep 1/4 bends, wyes, or combination tee-wyes for horizontal drainage transitions. Correct fitting selection ensures proper flow velocity and prevents waste accumulation.
